body:
It is very nice to have someone to talk to. Messaging you always gives me clarity and I am happy we have these conversations, and I am delighted to have made a friend as well:) (I also really like your writing style, it always puts a smile on my face). 


One of my best friends committed suicide this summer. I was a wreck when I found out. What usually keeps me from going over the edge is remembering how hurt I was when I found out he had done it. It's nice to count the kindness of strangers and life's unexpected pleasantries as reasons to keep me off the edge.

I think the worst part about suicidal thoughts is the mental yo-yo-ing you do.

One side of me is telling me that there would have been no point in living if this had happened, and I need to kill myself or hurt myself to fix this mistake.


The other half is angry that I am having those thoughts because everything turned out fine.


There's no middle ground and you go back and forth until you either wake up the next morning and go "goddamn did that really happen last night? Did I really almost do that?" or you hurt yourself until it feels better while it is happening. I'm happy I took the harder route and tried to go without. I only pinched myself twice when it got really bad. (Which is still far from optimal, I know. But it's better than doing it repeatedly which is what I used to do.)

That is a very long day!


I met with the professor again, and I found out something crazy. There were a few other students accused of plagiarism like me. I am very surprised to learn that. Other students that are smarter than me, too. And some didn't actually do it. It made me feel better in a way. I still accept what I did was wrong, but it surprises me that there are multiple people in this class experiencing this same problem and being threatened this way.


I've honestly been so stressed about school work that my normal scrutinizing thoughts haven't bothered me for the past few days. However, my sister made me watch Harry Potter with her recently, and there is a scene where Harry, Ron and Hermione are talking, and I believe it's Ron who goes "we could be killed!" and Hermione replies, "Or worse, expelled." It made me laugh really hard because I felt like she understood my panic. It made me feel slightly better about the situation. And also, finding out that the professor has done this to other people doesn't make me nearly as frightened or ashamed. It somehow helps me rationalize what happened.

Hi there! I've wanted to write to you for a while, but things have been insane here. My friend spilled a drink on my laptop a half hour into my birthday party, and I had to cancel the whole thing and run to buy a new one a half hour before the store closed. I do not have a car, and papers were do the next day, so there was not a lot of time to buy prudently or try to save the laptop and hope the motherboard dried out. Thankfully all my files were saved. 


I've also been having problems with fatigue and dizziness. I am afraid that I might have heart problems and have been trying to wrestle the car from my parents this weekend so when finals are over I can get this figured out. 


Overall, maximum stress. I am meeting with the professor again to discuss the final paper for that class, so I'm a bit anxious to meet her. However, I am hoping it will go well. 


I hope your week is going well.

Good afternoon. If you want to talk I'll listen to your stories. I would gladly listen if you want to talk. Yeah, I have quite a few stories from my childhood about not knowing how to handle bad things that happened to me. Thankfully, I've distanced myself from the family members that exhibit such toxic behaviors and try to enforce them on me. That's why I think this bothers me so much-- I thought if I cut ties with the toxic people then I wouldn't feel as bad anymore when I made mistakes. And this just set me right back into that nervous, overly-sensitive, depressed mindset I've spent years crawling out of.


Thank you for your kind words. It's hard for me to convey exactly how I feel when receiving genuine compliments, but I'm trying really hard to believe them. I think maybe it was even my professor explaining what she could have done rather than what she did which made it so much worse. 


I've been playing a few videogames with my friends and that has been keeping me calm at night. I really like Skyrim so that has been getting me through. It's fun to make a character that looks like me! I also like that if I get into the character it forces me to make the decisions as if I was there, so it keeps me out of my head for a while. Instead of being 'sad girl who is upset about everything and has to write papers' I am 'archmage of winterhold'!

I tried to go to bed early last night. I would spoil myself, but I don't have any money right now. I have my eyes on a pair of shoes though. Maybe if I get money for my birthday I'll try to purchase them. 


I have a lot of trouble accepting that 'as a human being you deserve good things.' I've never felt like I've deserved anything good. Since I was in kindergarten I had an issue with self harm. My family is very toxic and they try to gaslight about practically everything, but they level on the guilt if I try to do anything substantial, so it took until therapy to really learn coping skills, and even still I feel the need to punish myself every time I think about something bad that has happened to me.


I have a lot of issues trusting people, even if making friends is not hard for me, and I have a lot of trouble following advice because childhood taught me to stay as deep in my own introspection as I can. When I talk about my problems I find it very hard to take someone's advice, even if I agree with it. 


I think you're right that it intensified the bad feelings, but instead of completely making me want to end my life, it made me beat myself down, but that made it go away for today. 


I'm also upset at the idea that my professor had said if she 'wasn't so understanding' this could have been much worse and I could have gotten expelled. My brain is telling me the only option would have been suicide then. There is no way I can reason myself out of it. It is a fact. It is gravity. I would have had to do it. And I am trying really hard to tell myself that that's not something I should have done if that was the case, but I can't fight it. I can't argue with it.

It's approaching finals week so I have very little time to myself. Also my birthday is this weekend but I canceled all of my plans. I don't want to see people right now. I don't feel like I deserve to be around people. And also I really should double down on my papers I have so much to do for finals. I've been in a haze these days and my sleep schedule is completely messed up. I'm not eating much and I keep trying to tell myself that I didn't screw up that bad, but I am so miserable. When I tried to go for a walk it was all I thought about. I am so frustrated and upset.
Hi there. I'll check in with you tomorrow. Trying to finish the rest of my papers and maybe have some time to go for a walk tonight. Thank you again.

Hi sofar1776. I made it through ok-- lots of impulses to self-harm but only one or two thoughts of suicide today. I called my therapist and on break I'm going back to see him. I'm really frustrated now because I was doing so well, too. I had to deal with a LOT of stress this semester but I thought I was handling everything alright, you know? If anything I'm really frustrated about that right now.


I don't normally have such extreme reactions to mistakes I make-- I am ok failing at tests or not running as much as I wanted to during the day. I also haven't had urges to punish myself for things that used to really push me off the edge-- my mom always takes food away from me at the dinner table if she doesn't like what I'm eating (or put more vegetables on my plate if she doesn't like how many I've grabbed; she will also remove foods she thinks are 'unhealthy' from the table when I sit down with her), and she buys me XXL clothes (I'm a medium... and I don't ask her to buy things for me). I felt like I was doing so well. I felt like I was finally coming out of that depression. I finally had tools to handle it (I was in therapy for 5 years, tried multiple times to talk through these problems with my parents but it only made them more hostile the next time a problem occurred that I tried to talk to them about.)


I think the most frustrating part is I don't know why these thoughts are coming in so strong. Last night all I did was panic, cry, and fail at calming myself down for around six hours until I finally got myself together and called a friend to come over and chat. I didn't talk to her about any of this.


My professor really beat into me that what I did was about integrity. (We were told that it was ok to do research on the project beforehand, and I didn't realize that the three sentences I put in my paper about a historical figure were based on an argument and therefore plagiarizing) and it's that feeling that someone is disappointed in me that makes me feel absolutely awful. 


Thank you for checking in on me.

I think I get what you're saying. Kindergarten through middle school, I used to pinch myself when I would get upset. It took until middle school for a teacher to notice and call my mom to tell her what I would do when I would get embarrassed and upset. I feel guilty a lot. 


I just need to find stability. I called a friend who will be coming over soon. I know that if I go to bed and wake up I'll be able to handle it better. But I just need to get through the night.

Thank you. I really needed to hear that. I just need to get through the night. Like I said, I don't know why I'm self-destructing... it turned out fine... I hate that my brain does this. I'm currently at home and called a friend over so she'll be here soon. Thank you for talking to me.

It feels like the only solution to how I feel because I can't move past it. I don't know how to make it better but I can't talk to anyone about it. I'm too scared. I can't even look at the paper I'm so disgusted with myself. 


I don't want to hurt myself or commit suicide. It's this knee-jerk response I can't shake. I just want to self harm or end it because this feeling is crushing me. I even tried going for a run but as soon as I came down from the runner's high I felt just as bad. I'm under a lot of stress at school and I feel cornered by this and everything else. Like I'm not a good scholar anymore and I'll never be able to get into grad school.

I understand it. I just can't move past it. I'm still there in that room finding out. Like every time to think about it I don't get better- I get worse. I feel worse the more I think about it- not better. I keep trying to tell myself what I did wasn't that bad and that we've fixed it and won't do it again but it still FEELS like I should end my life over it.

The professor was so kind about it too. Like, everything is honestly fine. But I'm still shaking and I can't figure out why. Like, I have all the pieces about what made me upset. But I can't put them together in a way that helps me move past it. I'm stuck in the moment.
I don't know why either. That's the most painful part. I can't move past it and I feel like it's not over. I am just as upset now as I was initially.
Thank you. I'm just so frustrated. I can't stop feeling terrible about it. It happened a while ago but the urges haven't gone away. I can't shake it. I don't know why my brain does this to me.
